subject: K8s storage tiering, nodepool zoning and IOPS requirements for on-prem deployment

Subject: K8s storage / nodepool question for on-prem plan

Hi Sean —

Thanks again for walking us through the private deployment options yesterday. The infra team dug into the preliminary hardware profile and we have two open questions before we lock the node profiles:

1) For model-serving nodes (g4/g5-class equivalent), can we use local NVMe ephemeral for KV cache + checkpointing, or do you recommend always using network PVs for durability? We are concerned about failover and how Redwood recommends warming caches after node replacement.

2) For lower-cost batch inference nodes, what's the recommended disk IOPS baseline (read/write) per vGPU? We attached a short snapshot of our current test runs (bluewave-iops-snapshot.xlsx).

Also — we'd like a quick sketch of a nodepool zoning pattern (control plane, gpu-serve, batch, infra) that includes taints/tolerations and a suggestion for eviction priorities. Can you share a one-page recommendation we can include in the RFP?

--Carlos

Subject: Re: K8s storage / nodepool question for on-prem plan

Carlos —

Appreciate the questions and the IOPS snapshot. Short answers up front:

- NVMe ephemeral: acceptable for the KV cache layer and short-lived checkpoints if you have a fast rebuild process and a controller that can rehydrate cache from a central S3-compatible backing store. For anything you cannot afford to lose (model artifacts, audit logs, persistent replay buffers) use network-mounted PVs backed by your on-prem storage array.

- IOPS baseline: for batch nodes we recommend planning for 500–1,000 read IOPS and 200–500 write IOPS per vGPU as a starting point. For high-concurrency tokenized workloads, expect spikes; we typically size IOPS to observed 95th percentile from test runs (your spreadsheet helps).

I've attached a concise one-page recommendation and a proposed nodepool zoning diagram (proposed-nodepool-zoning-diagram.pdf) that shows:
- control-plane (3x, tainted, no GPU)
- gpu-serve (hot; local NVMe for KV cache + backing PVs for durable artifacts; taint: redwood/gpu=dedicated:NoSchedule)
- gpu-batch (cold; use network PVs, tolerates preemption; taint: redwood/gpu=batch:PreferNoSchedule)
- infra (logging, monitoring, registry; dedicated PVs with higher durability)

Eviction policy suggestion: prefer draining batch nodes first, then infra, preserve gpu-serve where possible. For cache rehydration, we recommend a startup hook that downloads hot prefixes from S3 and a background async prefetcher — this keeps 95th p99 cold-starts under target.

Next steps: can your team confirm whether the storage array can expose a fast NFS/CSI front-end, and whether you have an S3-compatible object store for cache warm-up? If yes, we can validate the exact IOPS per vGPU and produce final nodepool sizes.

Sean Gallagher

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: FW: K8s storage / nodepool question for on-prem plan

Quick bullets (from infra/runtime perspective):

- Bootstrap prefetch: for a 100M token KV store (~12GB gzipped hot prefixes), with a 1Gbps link the cold-warm time is ~2 minutes for initial prefix download if parallelized across 8 streams; with 10Gbps you get sub-30s. These numbers assume S3-compatible backend supports 8 concurrent GETs and low tail latency.
- Local NVMe tradeoffs: NVMe is excellent for low-latency KV access. Do not use ephemeral NVMe for single-copy model artifacts. For checkpoints, use ephemeral if you replicate checkpoints to durable object storage within N minutes (we can parameterize N; default 15m).
- IOPS: observed stats on our bench: heavy decoding loads produce sustained read bursts ~700–900 rIOPS per vGPU and write noise ~150–300 wIOPS. Recommend planning for 1,000 rIOPS headroom per vGPU and 500 wIOPS for safety in worst-case.
- K8s primitives: suggest nodeSelector labels: redwood/role={control,gpu-serve,gpu-batch,infra}; taints: redwood/role=gpu-serve:NoSchedule, redwood/role=gpu-batch:PreferNoSchedule. PodPriority: set gpu-serve pods > infra > batch.

I'll follow up with a short test script we can share for them to run on their storage to validate IOPS and bandwidth.

- Dev

Carlos / Priya —

Thanks for the prompt follow-up and for the spreadsheet. We've validated the numbers and attached a short guidance pack (redwood-onprem-storage-guidance-v1.pdf) and a test script you can run to measure IOPS/bandwidth on your arrays. TL;DR recommendations:

- Use local NVMe for KV cache + transient checkpointing when you can tolerate up to ~15 minutes of rebuild time and have an object-store-backed rehydrate path.
- Keep single-copy model artifacts and audit logs on durable network PVs with replication.
- Size IOPS for gpu-serve at 1,000 rIOPS / 500 wIOPS per vGPU (headroom included). For gpu-batch nodes, you can conservatively plan 500 rIOPS / 200 wIOPS per vGPU unless your batch jobs hit heavy IO.

Action items:
1) BlueWave: run the attached test script and send back the 95th percentile IOPS numbers (by Monday 4/19).
2) Redwood: we'll produce final nodepool sizing based on test results and produce Helm values examples for taints/PodPriority (target by 4/21).

If you want we can schedule a 30-minute runbook review next week to walk through failure scenarios (node replacement, array outage, network partition).

Best —
